## Key terms: three algorithms

<div style="font-size: 0.6em; line-height: 1.2;">

| Term | Meaning |
|:-----|:--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Manly-Jones (HRS-HCAP) algorithm** | The actuarial (rule-based) classification of HRS-HCAP 2016 participants as Normal, MCI, or Dementia (Manly et al., 2022). It uses five cognitive domains adjusted for age, sex, race, ethnicity, and education in a robust norms group (a subsample free of conditions that affect cognition), plus informant reports and self-rated memory concerns. It is the primary comparator in this work. |
| **(HRS) core algorithm** | The Manly-Jones algorithm adapted to HRS core data. One general cognition score from the Core tests, adjusted for the same demographic terms, replaces the five domains. Cut points, self-rated memory concerns, and the Jorm IQCODE (an informant questionnaire, used when cognitive tests are missing) assign the class. |
| **PMM** | Profile mixture model (based classification). A *pair* of statistical models calibrated to the Manly-Jones algorithm classes, using HRS Core cognitive tests, sociodemographic adjustment, self-reported memory concerns, and the Jorm IQCODE (among survey non-self-respondents). It gives each person a probability of being Normal, MCI, or Dementia. |

</div>
